stemMarkdown: A can do a job in 12 days. B is 100% more efficient than A. How many days does B take to do the same job alone? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Being 100% more efficient means B works at $200\%$ of A's rate, so B takes $\dfrac{100}{200}$ of A's time: $12 \times \dfrac{100}{200} = 6.0$ days.
altSolutionMarkdown: Efficiency and time are inversely related — more efficient means proportionally fewer days.
